engine noun

a motor

also engines, motor, car engine, diesel engine, petrol engine

modern

Traupman 216, 217, 310

mōtrum, mōtrī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an engine, a motor

Traupman’s word for the engine of a car; a diesel engine is Dīseliānum mōtrum (Traupman 216). It is not in Lewis & Short.

Other words

  • māchināmentum, māchināmentī n. — an engine

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 216, 310; Liv. 24.34 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Traupman gives it first for an engine. Classically a machine or engine of war, also a surgical instrument (Liv., Tac., Cels., Lewis & Short), so on its own it does not say motor.

  • mōtōrium, mōtōriī n. — a motor

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 217 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • Mōtrum autoraedae strepit; aliquid fractum est.

    The car’s engine is making a noise; something’s broken.composed

  • Dīseliānum mōtrum

    a diesel engineTraupman 216

See also car, machine, mechanic, fuel, petrol, fire engine, mechanism.
